title: Pocket Conductor — feature rundown (scratch)
content:
Notes to self / brain dump — Pocket Conductor (working name)

Goal: lightweight client-side feature that coordinates per-request fidelity, routing, and local prefetch hints to reduce cost while preserving perceived latency for end-user flows. Think of it as a small orchestrator that surfaces two things to apps: a) an affordable default lane and b) a fast-fallback path when quality matters.

Motivation
- Many apps want deterministic cost but still need occasional high-fidelity generations.
- Current global routing policies are coarse (per-customer or per-route). App-level hints could save tokens and improve UX.
- We can reduce waste by letting the app specify cheap-first patterns with automatic escalation.

Core concepts
- Fidelity lanes: tiny, standard, quality
  - tiny = quantized small model / cached prefix, best for short factual replies
  - standard = mainline hosted model with default quantization
  - quality = larger model or higher-temp sampling for creative tasks
- Escalation policy: threshold-based (confidence score, token budget, latency) or explicit (tool call requested)
- Local prefetch hints: client sends short prefix primes to warm KV cache on selected nodes (opt-in)

User stories
- As a product engineer, I want default low-cost responses for micro-queries and automatic upscale for follow-ups so monthly inference spend is predictable.
- As an assistant UX owner, I want manual "Prioritize quality" toggle on composer so power users can force quality lane for a session.
- As an SRE, I want to see lane-specific telemetry (P50/P95 latency, token units, escalations) instrumented so we can validate savings.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- SDK flag + HTTP header supporting lane selection and escalation hints
- Server-side routing applies lane -> model mapping (tiny->mnu-small, standard->mnu-medium, quality->mnu-large)
- Basic escalation: if first response score < threshold, automatically retry on next lane with preserved conversation context (<=1 retry)
- Telemetry emitted per-request with lane tag and escalation boolean

Metrics to track
- % of requests served in tiny/standard/quality
- Average cost per request and cost delta vs baseline
- Escalation rate and latency penalty for escalations
- User opt-in rate for manual quality toggle (beta)

Technical considerations
- KV warming: implemented as an optional prefetch handshake that populates remote cache but must be throttled (abuse risk)
- Idempotency: retries on escalation must not double-bill; use dedupe keys and server-side idempotency window
- Privacy: prefetch hints might include partial user context — require opt-in and encryption in transit; consider limiting to hashed tokens
- Routing integration: tie into smart-routing policies; allow Dedicated customers to pin lane mappings to their Dedicated pools

Open questions / risks
- How to compute a cheap/confidence score cheaply on tiny lane responses? (heuristics vs lightweight classifier)
- Billing model: do we bill per-attempt or per-successful-token? (affects cost-savings messaging)
- UX: when to surface "was this good?" to collect signals for escalation tuning without degrading UX
- Abuse vectors for KV prefetching and possible attack surface on cache population

Rollout plan (sketch)
- Phase 0: internal alpha (console + SDK) — instrument telemetry and run synthetic workloads to calibrate thresholds
- Phase 1: partner beta with 3 customers (one PLG startup, one mid-market, one enterprise dedicated) — gather cost/latency delta
- Phase 2: opt-in self-serve feature in Console + quickstart SDK snippets

Next steps (short list)
- Draft minimal SDK API surface (header names, env var, toggle) — owner: Omar (this doc)
- Spike: lightweight confidence heuristic on tiny lane (PoC by Eng Applied ML) — owner: Mika
- Telemetry schema PR to observability team (tags: pocket_conductor/lane/escalation) — owner: Lena

Quick sketch of SDK usage (pseudo)
- client = RedwoodClient({ pocketConductor: { defaultLane: 'tiny', allowEscalation: true } })
- generate({ prompt, pcHints: { expectedTokens: 40, manualPriority: false } }) -> returns { lane: 'tiny', escalated: false, costUnits }

Parking lot / ideas for future
- Lane scoring ML model that predicts when to skip tiny and go straight to standard
- Per-user saved preferences (power-user profiles) surfaced in Console
- Visual diff preview when escalating (show both tiny and quality outputs to help tuning)

Final note: keep MVP minimal. Focus on clear telemetry so we can prove unit-economics. This is directionally high ROI if we can push ~30% of low-value queries into tiny lane without increasing user friction.
